prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator switches after state check + Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log; go/no-go tracking. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale, replenishment forecasts. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner; Metocean Buoy local reference. Uncertain=constraint/no-go; Blade Inspection Drone deferred. Vessel Master authority proceed/hold/withdraw; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. CTV (Harness Audit Card), Daughter Craft, SOV (Recovery Basket Load Sheet); Marine Coordinator. North/South Access Scanner, Personnel Tracking Console; discrepancy pauses transfers. SCADA Engineer verifies Firmware Hash Attestation. Emergency: Rescue Coordinator, Field Supervisor, HSE Officer; Control Engineer remote shutdown; mode Turbine Lockout. Inventory: Warehouse System authoritative; Spares Hub; Storekeeper reconciles, records unavailable qty+next supply date. Replenishment requests (qty, need date, location, handling); low-stock alerts; work-window shortage→Duty Planner; substitutions need engineering acceptance; segregate damaged/expired; urgent purchases authorized, traceable; dispatch record; returns inspected. Isolation boundary approved (points, positions, responsible person, adjacent energized); Work Permit Portal publishes to

New part:
S722: Each isolation device is secured against unintended operation using the site-approved locking and tagging method.
S723: Personal protection is applied in accordance with the permit and local electrical safety rules.
S724: Electrical absence-of-voltage checks are performed at the work location using suitable, tested equipment.
S725: Stored energy, induced voltage, and other hazardous energy sources are assessed before hands-on work begins.
S726: The Field Supervisor confirms that every crew member understands the limits of the approved work area.
S727: Changes to the task, equipment state, or work location require a review of the boundary before work continues.
S728: The Work Permit Portal retains the current approval and makes superseded versions unavailable for active work.
S729: Control room staff and the field team use the same revision when confirming isolation status.
S730: A shift handover records outstanding isolations, affected equipment, and any restrictions that remain in force.
S731: The incoming team independently checks the boundary status before accepting responsibility for ongoing work.
S732: No isolation is removed until the work is complete, personnel and tools are accounted for, and the responsible authority approves restoration.
S733: The person removing each control confirms that the associated work party is clear of the hazard area.
S734: The Control Engineer verifies the restoration state and communicates any remaining operational limitation to affected personnel.
S735: Boundary records are closed only after the equipment state has been confirmed and the permit has been updated.
S736: Substation switching windows are coordinated with planned maintenance so that equipment is available only when the required operating conditions can be maintained.
S737: The Duty Planner consolidates proposed work periods and identifies tasks that require a change to substation configuration.
S738: The Maintenance Planning Engine checks task durations, dependencies, and resource assumptions before a window is proposed.
S739: The Grid Dispatcher confirms that the requested period is compatible with export requirements and network operating limits.
S740: The approved window includes a start time, an end time, the affected equipment, and the expected operating state.
S741: The Substation Operator reviews the switching sequence and confirms that each step can be performed within the available interval.
S742: The Control Engineer checks that turbine operations can be managed safely while the substation work is in progress.
S743: The Grid Interface Relay remains available for the required protection and control functions throughout the planned work.
S744: Work on the Main Transformer is scheduled only after its expected loading and required isolation duration have been reviewed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
